ApiKeyHeader.description:
Authentication token for accessing the API. API tokens are of the form 'token AT1.xyz' and you can locate them under your profile settings page (top-right -> Settings -> API Tokens).
Note: if you are already logged in to the service through a browser, you do not need to provide a valid token to interact with the endpoints, but this parameter will be required if you attempt to access the same endpoint through another method like curl.
ApiKeyHeader.name: X-Mayhem-Token

200.description:
Get defects for a owner, optionally filtered by project/target.

    The target to filter on is determined by the target slug passed in the query
    parameter `target`.

    The run to filter on is determined by the run number passed in the query
    parameter `run`. A value of "latest" here will return defects for the most
    recent run based on the run's created_at time.

    Pagination defaults to 10 per page and starts on offset 0.

    :param owner: the owner
    :param offset: the offset of the results to retrieve, 0-indexed
    :param per_page: how many results to retrieve per page
    :param project: an optional filter on the project
    :param target: an optional filter on the target
    :param run: an optional filter on the run number
    :param defect_type: an optional filter on the defect CWE number
    :param branch_name: an optional filter used to select the defect state for the
                        given branch. If not specified, the Project default branch
                        is used.
    :param no_branch: an explicit boolean that filters defect state details to
                      runs without branch information. When this is true,
                      branch_name cannot be set.

    :returns: A dict where the `defects` key contains a list of the desired defects

200.description:
Updates a single target from a owner.

    URL updates are only valid for API targets. Clients may archive or
    unarchive any target type by setting is_archived true/false. This
    does not soft-delete the target or trigger GC.

    Archive / unarchive (setting ``is_archived``) uses this same endpoint and
    therefore the same ``PROJECT_ADMIN`` authorization as other target updates.
    Callers without project admin access are rejected with 404 (NotFound),
    matching other PROJECT_ADMIN-gated routes.

    Returns:
        The updated target on success

201.description:
Create a pending test-connection record for (owner, project, target).

    The client may supply the ``uuid`` used as the row's primary key; if omitted, one
    is generated here. The service layer runs the 2-minute sweep, the in-flight guard,
    and the insert (see ai/requirement.md AC-01/AC-02/AC-10-AC-12). ``base_url`` is
    validated by the schema but intentionally not persisted (AC-03); ``_org``/
    ``_subscription`` are injected by ``plan_from_route`` only so the quota gate
    (AC-09) runs -- neither is used here, and no ``RunCount`` is ever written.

200.description:
Fetch one test connection by uuid for the caller (creator), scoped to the URL's
    (owner, project, target).

    Five-way ``one_or_404`` on ``(id, owner, project, target, started_by)`` -- a
    foreign uuid, tenant, or creator all collapse to the same 404 (see
    ai/requirement.md AC-04/AC-05). Results are omitted (and unqueried) while the
    parent is TEST_PENDING and returned ordered by ``sequence`` once terminal
    (AC-01/AC-02).

201.description:
Bulk-insert per-endpoint results and derive the overall verdict.

    Ownership scoping (the row's project/target must match the URL's authorized
    ``project_slug``/``target_slug``, not just ``owner``), the TEST_PENDING guard, the
    size cap, and the verdict derivation + finalize all happen atomically in the
    service layer (AC-14/AC-15/AC-18). An empty ``results`` finalizes nothing -- the
    parent stays TEST_PENDING (AC-13). No webhook / post_process_run (AC-17).
